✦ Hihihi! 🌱

I'm Xiaojing Du (杜晓静), a second-year PhD student at the University of Cambridge, supervised by Professor Brechtje Post and Professor Francis Nolan.

My research explores how we produce and perceive speech, especially the creaky endings of tones in Huoji Jin Chinese.

How do the physical signals we measure relate to what listeners actually hear? Can we teach computers to recognise different voice qualities, even across languages? And how much of our voice comes from biology, and how much from the languages we speak?

These are some of the questions I'm curious about and excited to explore! ✨

📄 Publications

Interspeech 2026

The Role of Phonation Type in Chinese Jin Tones: A Study Using Acoustic Metrics

Du, X., Nolan, F., & Post, B.

Interspeech 2026

Tonal convergence in Huoji (Jin Chinese) compresses f0 space, so T1 and T5 overlap when the checked tone's glottal constriction weakens late-vowel f0. Comparing Praat, YIN, and REAPER trackers, we show that f0-only measures keep T5 nearest T1, but adding HNR05 and H1*–H2* separates them, since phonation-sensitive measures complement f0 when periodicity is locally unreliable.

Conference Talk · 2026

Segmental vs. Suprasegmental Glottalization in a Jin Chinese Dialect: Phonetic Pathways of Tone and Phonation

Du, X., Nolan, F., & Post, B.

International Conference on Phonetic Variation 2026, University of Granada

Examines how glottalization operates at both the segment and the suprasegmental (tone) level in a Jin Chinese dialect, tracing the phonetic pathways linking tone and phonation.

🔭 Research & Events

Ongoing Projects

Voice Quality and Tone in Jin Chinese

University of Cambridge · 2025 – Present
  • Investigating phonation type in Jin Chinese tones, contributing speech-science evidence from an under-studied Sinitic variety.
  • Analysing F0, duration, HNR, H1–H2, CPP, and frame-level voice quality measures alongside SSL-derived probes.
In Progress

Interpretable Voice Quality Labelling

University of Cambridge · Interdisciplinary · 2026 – Present
  • Voice quality terminology is fragmented across linguistics, clinical, and engineering fields, and this project works toward a shared, reusable frame-level voice quality detector.
  • Funded by the Cambridge Language Sciences Incubator Fund ("Hearing Every Voice: Interpretable Voice Quality Labelling for Inclusive AI").
In Progress

Huoji Tone Perception: Further Data Collection

University of Cambridge · Fieldwork: Henan, China · 2026 – Present
  • Collecting further perception data on the Huoji dialect to test whether listeners rely on F0, phonation, or both to distinguish the T1–T5 tone contrast, replicating and extending Lu et al.'s methodology.
  • Aims toward a complete production-and-perception picture of the Huoji dialect.
In Progress
